analysis.evidence: נֹחַ is the subject of וַיּוֹלֶד. The object שְׁלֹשָׁה בָנִים means “three sons,” whom the verse names as Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ and no suffix

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for נֹחַ linked to the root article nuach.
draft.definition: Noah, the son whom Lamech names in hope of relief from toil.
draft.evidence: Genesis 5:29 gives the name נֹחַ and explains it through the wordplay on יְנַחֲמֵנוּ, “he will comfort us.”

analysis.evidence: נֹחַ is the subject of וַיּוֹלֶד, “he fathered.” The verse names his three sons as Shem, Ham, and Japheth, identifying him as the same Noah whom Lamech named in Genesis 5:29.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name in the absolute state, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: שְׁלֹשָׁה counts the masculine plural בָנִים. The verse names Noah’s three sons individually: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
אֶת marks שֵׁם (Shem) as the first of the three sons named as objects of וַיּוֹלֶד ‘he fathered’. The marker recurs before חָם and יָפֶת.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected direct-object marker with no prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add Genesis 10:21 to the existing personal-name article as evidence identifying Shem.
draft.definition: Shem, one of Noah’s sons, brother of Japheth and ancestor of Eber’s descendants.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:21 identifies Shem by his relationship to Japheth and to Eber’s descendants.

analysis.evidence: The verse says that Noah fathered three sons and names them in order, each with its own direct-object marker. שֵׁם is the first son listed, followed by חָם and יָפֶת.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun without a prefix or suffix. The preceding אֶת is a separate direct-object marker.
analysis.sense: Shem, son of Noah and brother of Japheth

analysis.evidence: אֶת introduces חָם (Ham), the second of the three sons named as objects of וַיּוֹלֶד (‘he fathered’). The marker appears before each son’s name.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected direct-object particle without prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Clarify the existing Genesis 9:18 evidence note by identifying Ham’s place in the list at the first occurrence.
draft.definition: Ham, son of Noah and father of Cush, Mizraim, Put and Canaan.
draft.evidence: Genesis 9:18 first names Ham among Noah’s sons and then identifies him as Canaan’s father.

analysis.evidence: The verse says Noah fathered three sons. It names each with a direct-object marker, and אֶת חָם identifies Ham as the second son listed, between Shem and Japheth.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name with no prefix or suffix. The preceding direct-object marker אֶת is a separate word.
analysis.sense: Ham, son of Noah and father of Canaan

draft.change: Add Genesis 6:10 as an example under the existing definite-object sense of אֵת in et.
draft.definition: Introduces a definite direct object, including a proper name in a coordinated list.
draft.evidence: Genesis 6:10 repeats אֶת before each of Noah’s three sons’ names. In וְאֶת יָפֶת the conjunction joins Japheth to Shem and Ham.

analysis.evidence: In אֶת שֵׁם אֶת חָם וְאֶת יָפֶת, each name has its own object marker. The three names identify the שְׁלֹשָׁה בָנִים, “three sons,” whom Noah fathered. At the marked occurrence, וְ־ introduces the final name and אֶת marks יָפֶת as the third son.
analysis.morphology: Prefixed coordinating conjunction וְ־ “and” + unsuffixed definite direct-object marker אֶת.

analysis.evidence: The verse says Noah fathered three sons. The direct-object marker introduces each name in turn, and וְאֶת יָפֶת identifies Japheth as the third son listed, after Shem and Ham.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name in pausal form יָפֶת, with no prefix or suffix.
